newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds hold fire against fragile U.S..
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds hold fire against fragile U.S..

text.p: *Australian bonds turned quiet after an initial burst of activity in the futures pit with domestics already seen short, limiting the impact of Monday's further slide in the U.S.
*First leg of U.S. refunding auctions due later on Tuesday.

Australian bonds turned quiet after an initial burst of activity in the futures pit with domestic institutions already seen short of stock and limiting the impact of Monday's further slide in U.S. Treasuries.
Positive fundamentals also helped to underpin the local market, which supported a compression of the spread differential to the U.S. at the longer end of the curve, traders said.

"The domestics have been very quiet. I think they are short of stock, and if anything, the offshore is overweight," one trader said. "The key event is Thursday's employment numbers, which will decide whether the bill strip is overpriced or not."

Since last Wednesday's 1/2 point cut in official interest rates September and December bill futures have been trading below the new cash rate of 5.0 percent and Thursday's labour force data could prove to be one of the early indicators to suggest whether a further policy easing is on the cards.
Before then, the U.S. will provide the main backdrop for local activity and where the quarterly refunding auctions get underway later on Tuesday.
The US$38.0 billion refunding starts with US$16.0 billion of three-year notes today, then US$12.0 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday and US$10.0 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday.

Ten-year bonds outperformed against the U.S., putting support at 25 basis points under pressure and the lowest level since the early 1980s. The Canadian bond market was closed on Monday. The short end of the New Zealand curve weakened after its employment report was stronger than expected.
